        "content": "Spring AI is a Spring-based framework for building AI-powered applications in Java and Kotlin. It aims to make it easier to integrate large language models (LLMs), embeddings, vector databases, and other AI services into Spring Boot apps using familiar Spring patterns.

## What it gives you

Spring AI provides abstractions and integrations for things like:

- **Chat models**: talk to LLMs such as OpenAI, Anthropic, Azure OpenAI, Ollama, etc.
- **Embeddings**: turn text into vectors for search and retrieval
- **Vector stores**: store and query embeddings in systems like pgvector, Redis, Pinecone, Milvus, and others
- **Prompt engineering**: build prompts and manage templates
- **RAG (Retrieval-Augmented Generation)**: combine your own data with model responses
- **Tool/function calling**: let models call external tools or functions
- **Audio/image support**: depending on provider and module support
- **Observability and testing**: integrate with Spring Boot tooling and testing patterns

## Why people use it

If you already know Spring Boot, Spring AI helps you avoid writing provider-specific code everywhere. It gives you a more consistent API so you can:

- swap model providers more easily
- connect to your own data for grounded answers
- build chatbots, assistants, search apps, and automation tools
- keep your app structure aligned with normal Spring development

## Typical use cases

- Internal knowledge base chatbot
- Customer support assistant
- Semantic search over documents
- Content generation
- Code assistant
- Agent-like workflows with tools and memory

## Example idea

A common Spring AI app flow looks like:

1. User asks a question
2. App retrieves relevant documents from a vector store
3. App sends question + context to an LLM
4. LLM returns an answer grounded in your data

That’s the core of RAG.

## Basic example

A simplified Spring AI-style usage might look like:

```java
@RestController
class ChatController {

    private final ChatClient chatClient;

    ChatController(ChatClient.Builder builder) {
        this.chatClient = builder.build();
    }

    @GetMapping("/chat")
    String chat(@RequestParam String message) {
        return chatClient.prompt()
                .user(message)
                .call()
                .content();
    }
}
```

## Status and ecosystem

Spring AI is part of the Spring ecosystem and is evolving quickly. Since AI tooling changes fast, the project tends to focus on:
- clean abstractions
- provider integrations
- Spring Boot auto-configuration
- production-friendly patterns

## When to choose it

Spring AI is a good fit if:
- you’re already using Spring Boot
- you want Java/Kotlin support
- you need LLM integration with enterprise-style app structure
- you want RAG or vector search without building everything from scratch
